summary.intent: Decide whether to add a chat channel (MS Teams or Telegram) for buyer alerts in the ask-soony hackathon project, inspired by how askLio works inside Teams, and have the assistant build it.
summary.outcome: Built a one-way Teams integration (Adaptive Card posted via a Workflows webhook, buttons linking into the app's /d/<id> page) in src/ask_soony/teams.py, wired into the router, background loop and supplier-reply follow-up, with tests against a local webhook stand-in. The full suite passed (169/169) and the work was committed; the real Teams webhook is not yet created.

repo: Teams alerts are configured via ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK and toggled with ASK_TEAMS=on in .env; the background loop reads the flag at startup, so it must also be honored when set in .env.
Existing alert channels are phone push, phone call for critical cases, and email to suppliers; Teams adds the missing chat channel.
Approve and voice actions already exist in the app at /d/<id>, so the Teams card only needs to deep-link there instead of implementing a bot.
Adaptive Cards only support a fixed set of colour names, so colour logic had to be mapped to those.
Challenge data is confidential, and a Teams post sends supplier names and numbers to the Microsoft tenant, so a team-only or demo-only channel is recommended.

code.finding: New module that builds the Adaptive Card (headline, SAP says / document says, Approve and Open evidence buttons) and posts it to the Teams Workflows webhook.

workflow: Testing against a local stand-in for an external webhook lets integration work proceed before credentials exist.
Shared test fixtures belong in conftest.py; importing them across test files tripped lint.

Tests were loading the developer's real .env, which caused unexpected 401s from the password protection in unrelated tests. Bisecting which test file leaked the env led to isolating tests from the real .env.
Run lint and the full test suite before committing.

friction: Moving the shared fixture to conftest.py caused 401 failures in other tests because the real .env leaked into the test process, which took several debugging steps to find.
Lint objected to the shared fixture import in the first test layout.
Time pressure: it was about 3:00 with hand-in at 12:00, and Teams was the last feature before the PR merge, demo script, deck and video.
open_items: User must create the Teams Workflows webhook (Post to a channel when a webhook request is received) and put the URL in .env as ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK; the integration has only been tested against a local stand-in.
Decide which Teams account or channel to use, given the confidentiality of the challenge data.
Four commits for PR #5 are still waiting for the user's OK to push, followed by merging it.
Demo script, deck and video still to do before the 12:00 hand-in.
Two-way approval inside Teams via a real bot (Azure Bot registration, app manifest) was deliberately skipped as too risky.
Telegram bot was considered as a two-way alternative but not built.
